## Review Summary

This PR adds a Node.js/Vitest behavioral test harness for the `story-compaction` OpenCode plugin, introducing unit tests for five pure functions and integration tests for `assembleContext` with real filesystem fixtures. The implementation is clean and well-structured, with good edge-case coverage. The main concerns are around dependency version pinning in `package.json` and a missing trailing newline in `.gitignore`.

## Findings

### Critical Findings

None.

### Warning Findings

```
[W-01] Unpinned "latest" versions in package.json
Category: Correctness
Severity: Warning
File: package.json
Lines: 8-9
Description: Both `typescript` and `vitest` are specified as `"latest"` rather
  than pinned semver ranges. This means `npm install` on different machines or at
  different times can resolve to different major versions, potentially breaking
  tests or introducing incompatibilities. The committed `package-lock.json`
  provides de-facto pinning, but any `npm update` or fresh `npm install` without
  the lock file will pull whatever is newest.
Suggestion: Pin to semver ranges matching the versions currently in
  `package-lock.json`, e.g.:
    "typescript": "^5.8.3",
    "vitest": "^3.1.1"
  This preserves patch/minor updates while preventing unexpected major bumps.
```

```
[W-02] Missing trailing newline in .gitignore
Category: Style
Severity: Warning
File: .gitignore
Lines: 181
Description: The file does not end with a newline character (POSIX requirement).
  Some tools may behave unexpectedly with files lacking a trailing newline, and
  future appends via `echo "..." >> .gitignore` will concatenate onto the last
  line instead of adding a new entry.
Suggestion: Add a trailing newline after `node_modules/`.
```

### Suggestions

```
[S-01] Integration test uses long single-line writeFileSync calls
Category: Style
Severity: Suggestion
File: .opencode/plugins/__tests__/story-compaction.integration.test.ts
Lines: 39-44
Description: The wiki fixture file contents (frontmatter strings) are written as
  single long lines that exceed 120 characters, making the test setup harder to
  read and modify. This applies to the `writeFileSync` calls for `alice.md`,
  `main-quest.md`, and `chapter-1.md`.
Suggestion: Use template literals with proper line breaks for the fixture content,
  e.g.:
    writeFileSync(
      join(wikiDir, "characters", "alice.md"),
      [
        "---",
        "title: Alice",
        "role: protagonist",
        "detail_levels:",
        "  L1: A brave adventurer",
        "---",
        "Full character bio here.",
      ].join("\n"),
    );
```

```
[S-02] Consider adding beforeEach isolation for temp directory creation
Category: Testing
Severity: Suggestion
File: .opencode/plugins/__tests__/story-compaction.integration.test.ts
Lines: 8-22
Description: The temp directory management pattern (manual array + afterEach
  cleanup) works correctly but is duplicated across test setups. If additional
  integration test files are added in the future, extracting the temp directory
  helper into a shared fixture would reduce boilerplate. This is not urgent for a
  single test file.
Suggestion: No action needed now; note for future test expansion.
```

## Overall Assessment

The PR is ready for merge with minor fixes. The test harness is well-designed: unit tests cover each exported pure function with edge cases (empty input, missing frontmatter, path traversal attacks, undefined fields), and integration tests exercise the full `assembleContext` pipeline against real filesystem state including error paths (missing `state.json`, invalid JSON). The export block in `story-compaction.ts` is minimal and non-invasive — it only re-exports existing private functions without changing the default plugin export.

The `isWithinBase` path traversal tests are a welcome security verification. The `vitest.config.ts` and `tsconfig.json` are correctly scoped to the plugin directory. The only substantive issue is W-01 (unpinned versions), which should be addressed before merge to prevent future CI drift. W-02 (trailing newline) is a quick fix. Both suggestions are cosmetic and can be deferred.
